finding: Test 16 requires each numeric §7 field to accept both range endpoints and "reject one step outside each", but §7 states "Budget fields are decimal dollars" and gives no granularity for them. For `run_max_budget_usd` (0-10000) and `run_max_unit_budget_usd` (0-1000) "one step outside" is undefined: two engineers would assert rejection at 10001 vs 10000.01, and at -1 vs -0.01, and would disagree on whether an in-range fractional value such as 0.5 is accepted. The three integer fields (`run_max_units`, `run_max_wall_clock_seconds`, `run_max_unit_retries`) have an obvious step; the two decimal fields do not.

resolved.evidence: Accepted with recorded justification: two medium test-sharpness observations and one low. The second consecutive round in which no role produced a blocking finding, on an unchanged spec. Carried into implementation as task-level detail.

suggestion: Pin the rejection values explicitly in test 16 (or the precision in §7): e.g. state that budget fields are validated to two decimal places, so the rejected values are -0.01 and 10000.01 / 1000.01, and that a fractional value inside the range is accepted.

finding: Test 69 requires `tp config --resolved`, `tp config --extract` and `tp validate --project` to "each cover all seven new §7 fields", but §7 also says `notify_cmd` "is per-operator rather than per-project and is read from `.tp/local.json` only". What it means for `--extract` (which materializes project-config values) to cover a field that project config never supplies is not pinned — an assertion that `--extract` emits `notify_cmd` and one that it deliberately omits it are both defensible readings of the same sentence. §10.2 test 16 pulls the other way, asserting only that `notify_cmd` is read from `.tp/local.json`.

resolved.evidence: Accepted with recorded justification: two medium test-sharpness observations and one low. The second consecutive round in which no role produced a blocking finding, on an unchanged spec. Carried into implementation as task-level detail.

suggestion: State per command what "cover" means for `notify_cmd`: e.g. `--resolved` reports it, `--extract` omits it because it is not a project-config field, and `validate --project` errors when it appears in `.tp/config.json` — then reword test 69 as "all seven for `--resolved`, six for `--extract`" (or whichever split is intended).
